title: The Last Autumn of the Lake
subtitle: 气候变化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 气候变化（环境保护·气候变化）
meta: 主题语境：气候变化（环境保护·气候变化）　|　核心词汇：issue　|　正文 355 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 issue 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Nobody in my town talked about climate ten years ago. Then the lake behind the primary school dried to a bed of dust, and suddenly the question at ① issue was not whether the weather had changed but who should pay for it. Our teacher asked us to make it the theme of the term's wall newspaper.

We spent a week reading before we wrote a line. The December ② issue of a science magazine for young readers had a map that frightened us: temperatures rising throughout the province, rainfall falling by nearly a fifth. We borrowed the library's copy and photocopied the page, and we began to understand that this was an ③ issue far larger than our lake.

Then our group argued. My friend said we should ④ make an issue of the new factory on the hill, since its pipes ran straight into the stream. I ⑤ took issue with her: I did not believe the evidence was strong enough. That row lasted three afternoons, and in the end we wrote two pieces instead of one, side by side, so that readers could judge for themselves.

The local council later ⑥ issued a short statement saying that the lake would refill in the spring. The following week the water board ⑦ issued every household with a leaflet about saving water: shorter showers, buckets under the tap, no hosepipes before July. My grandmother laughed at the leaflet. She said she had practised all that for sixty years without being told, and every summer since she has issued the same advice to the neighbours herself.

The lake did refill, though nobody issued a promise that it would stay and it never reached its old level again. Last month our old teacher came back and asked what we had learned. I said I had learned to separate the big ⑧ issue from the small one, and that small ⑨ issues — a tap left running, a hose, a habit — are the only ones a student can actually settle. She said this was the best answer she had heard; probably she ⑩ issued the same praise to every class, but I have kept it anyway.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 问题；议题（环境议题、社会议题）
C. v. 发布；发表（声明、警告、命令）
D. v. 发给；配发（issue sb with sth）
E. 固定搭配：at issue 争论中的；待解决的
F. 固定搭配：make an issue of 把……当回事；大做文章
G. 固定搭配：take issue with 反对；不赞同
H. 固定搭配：issue sth to sb 向某人说／给某人（此处指给出评价）

items.q: the question at issue was not whether the weather had changed
The December issue of a science magazine
this was an issue far larger than our lake
we should make an issue of the new factory
issued every household with a leaflet
to separate the big issue from the small one
small issues — a tap left running
she issued the same praise to every class

answers.why: at issue 是固定搭配，意为“争论中的、待解决的”，此处指大家争论的焦点已换了。
December issue of a magazine 指杂志十二月那一期，是名词“期号”。
an issue far larger than our lake 指比湖泊大得多的“议题”，这正是名词“问题；议题”。
make an issue of sth 意为“把某事当回事、就某事大做文章”，朋友主张拿工厂做文章。
take issue with sb 意为“不同意某人”，与下句 I did not believe the evidence 相呼应。
issue a statement 是动词“发布、发表（正式声明）”，主语是地方议会。
issue sb with sth 意为“发给某人某物”，这里指给每户发节水宣传单。
the big issue 指大问题、大议题，与第 3 题同为名词“议题”。
small issues 与前面的 big issue 对比，指学生真正能解决的一件件小事。
issue sth to sb 本义“发给”，此处转义为“给出（同样的表扬）”，与前两处动词用法同源。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 争论的焦点已不是天气是否变了。（at issue）
我在那本科学杂志的十二月号上读到了它。（issue n.）
气候变化是一个比我们这个湖大得多的问题。（issue n.）
政府昨天发布了一份简短的声明。（issue v.）
社区给每户家庭都发了节水宣传单。（issue sb with）
我不同意她的看法，因为证据还不够。（take issue with）
answers: The question at issue was no longer whether the weather had changed.
I read about it in the December issue of that science magazine.
Climate change is an issue far larger than our lake.
The government issued a short statement yesterday.
The community issued every household with a leaflet about saving water.
I took issue with her because the evidence was not strong enough.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 issue 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: Nobody in our town discussed the climate until the lake dried to a bed of dust.
The question at issue was no longer whether the weather had changed, but who should pay for it.
In the December issue of a science magazine we found a map of temperatures rising throughout our province.
Later the council issued a statement, and every household was issued with a leaflet about saving water.
I took issue with my friend, though I am no longer sure I was right.
The big issue is beyond me, but small ones — a running tap, a hose in June — are what a student can settle.
